extracted.intended_audience: Authors submitting manuscripts to the Annals of Applied Probability (IMS journal)
extracted.subtask_description: Submission and manuscript-preparation guidelines for authors intending to submit papers to the Annals of Applied Probability, including procedural requirements (submission system, file types) and editorial policies (originality, arXiv history, supporting material).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission implies originality and author approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of a manuscript implies (a) that the same work has not been published before; (b) that it is not under consideration for publication elsewhere; and (c) that its publication has been approved by all co-authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must ensure the work is original, not under simultaneous consideration, and that all co-authors have approved submission. This is a condition of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of EJMS for submission
rubrics_metrics.description: The IMS uses The Electronic Journal Management System (EJMS) for submission and handling of papers by the editorial board and reviewers for its journals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should access https://www.e-publications.org/ims/submission/. If you are a first time user you must complete the registration. You are only required to register once. After the registration is complete you will have the ability to submit your manuscript. After completing the form you will then upload your PDF file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard copy submissions only in exceptional cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Hard copy submissions are acceptable only in the rare cases that computer facilities are not available to an author.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer electronic submission through EJMS; prepare hard-copy only when computer facilities are unavailable and only in truly rare circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: arXiv posting and arXiv history considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are encouraged to post their work on the arXiv before submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A long gap between arXiv and journal submission, or otherwise unusual arXiv history, inevitably leads to some editorial concern. In such cases authors may comment on the circumstances at submission. If the paper was previously rejected at similarly competitive journals, authors should consider carefully whether submission to AAP is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission of referenced/unpublished papers
rubrics_metrics.description: Unpublished or not easily available papers cited in the manuscript should be submitted with the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide these cited, unpublished, or hard-to-obtain references as supplementary files alongside the submission so referees and editors can access them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow detailed preparation instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please see detailed instructions on Preparation of Manuscripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors must follow the linked manuscript-preparation guidelines (formatting, length, style, etc.) provided by the journal; consult that page for specific formatting and submission-ready file requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of source files after acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: After a paper is accepted, you will be asked to provide Mattson Publishing Services with a LaTeX file of the final version of the paper, if one is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Other forms of TeX are acceptable if LaTeX is not available. You will also be asked to supply source files for figures (.eps or .jpg are preferred) along with a PDF file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Galley proofs and final corrections
rubrics_metrics.description: The corresponding author will receive email regarding galley proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The email will include instructions for returning corrections as well as links to forms required for publication. Follow those instructions promptly to complete publication steps.
